newsitem.title: NORWAY: SAS SHARES KEEP FLYING IN OSLO.
newsitem.headline: SAS SHARES KEEP FLYING IN OSLO.

text.p: The Oslo-quoted shares in Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) climbed almost six percent on Thursday after the company a day earlier beat market expectations with first-half results.
At 1026 GMT, SAS's B share stood 5.7 percent, or 6.50 crowns, up at 120.50 crowns in turnover of 19 million crowns.

On Wednesday the airliner, owned jointly by the governments of Norway, Sweden, Denmark and by shareholders, released second-quarter profits before tax at 1.38 billion crowns, more than double analysts' forecasts.
The results sent SAS shares up in Copenhagen, Stockholm and Oslo, where it closed nine crowns higher at 114 crowns.
